summary:
Chandra Yatra is a mission-planning app for the Moon's south pole that turns complex lunar science into one clear, actionable plan.
The south pole is rich in water-ice but brutally difficult to explore. Low Sun angles create long, fast-moving shadows. Permanently shadowed craters plunge to minus 180 degrees. The 14.8-day lunar night drains batteries. Steep slopes, hidden boulders, blocked radio signals, solar flares, moonquakes, and landing-blast plumes threaten crews and machines.
Chandra Yatra solves this in one app. Its lighting layer replays Sun and Earth on a 3D dome so planners can pick safe working windows. Its thermal layer maps cold traps and sizes fuel cells for the long night. Its terrain planner flags red zones and builds safe, low-energy routes. Its communications layer ray-traces the horizon and reroutes links through ridge towers. Its hazard layer maps blast radii and finds the nearest deep-regolith safe haven.
Finally, its siting optimizer compares fuel, ice, sunlight, and zone conflicts to rank the best base location. All findings come together inside the app into one auto-generated mission brief, ready to share.
Built on NASA LRO LOLA, Diviner, SPICE, and JPL Horizons data, Chandra Yatra is one app, one plan — your journey to the Moon.
details:
Chandra Yatra — Your Journey to the Moon's South Pole

Chandra Yatra is an intuitive web app for NASA's Artemis program. Missions to the Moon's south pole face extreme lighting, cold, terrain, communication, and hazard constraints, while existing tools are fragmented and complex. Chandra Yatra turns raw NASA ephemeris data into one clear, actionable plan.

What does it do and how does it work?

It integrates 29 problem-solving modules in one app:

Lighting and Communication: 3D Horizon Dome and ray-casting using LRO LOLA DEMs and JPL Horizons for Sun, Earth, shadows, and direct-to-Earth blackouts.
Site Comparison: Side-by-side matrices and an AI Landing Site Matchmaker.
Time Prediction: Minute-resolution Chrono-Scrubber, Safe Window Scheduler, and Shadow Flicker warnings.
Thermal and Energy: Diviner cold-trap mapping, Fission Surface Power siting, and Regenerative Fuel Cell balancing for the 14.8-day lunar night.
Terrain and Mobility: Slope risk above 15 degrees, CADRE swarm pathfinding, and IPEx regolith haul optimization.
Hazards and Safety: Solar flare safe-havens, dust blast radius, moonquake fatigue, electrostatic dust risk, and thermal cycling fatigue.
Siting and Operations: Zoning and Claim Clash resolver, delta-V and fuel optimizer, ice prospecting, ISRU Ice-to-Sun Score, mesh re-routing, and GPS-denied celestial localization.
Infrastructure: PROMISE wireless power, shadow conflict matrix, and cable-snag simulator.

All layers come together into one auto-generated mission proposal brief.

Benefits and impact:

It saves time, reduces human error and risk, and makes lunar planning accessible to scientists, students, and educators. It helps prevent tipping, battery failure, signal loss, and crew danger before launch, and supports outreach through AR Stand on the Moon WebXR mode.

Tools and technology:

Frontend: http://React.js / http://Vue.js, Tailwind CSS. 3D: CesiumJS / http://Three.js, WebXR. Backend: Python (FastAPI), NumPy, SciPy. GIS: GDAL, rasterio. Export: ReportLab / WeasyPrint.

NASA Datasets: LRO LOLA DEMs, LRO NAC, Diviner, ShadowCam, SPICE Kernels, JPL Horizons, Moon Base Challenge Specs (FSP, RFC, CADRE, IPEx, PROMISE, miniCAST), Volatile Maps, and Seismic Models.

Creativity:

Instead of showing raw data, we focused on decisions — what should a planner actually do? We combined safety, energy, communication, survival, fuel, and science into one journey: 29 problems, one app, one plan.
